extracted.intended_audience: Canadian patent applicants, patentees, and patent agents (representatives); practitioners who calculate additional term and manage transitional filing/prosecution issues
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for determining, certifying, reconsidering, and litigating additional patent term in Canada, and related transitional provisions for applications and prosecution arising from changes to the Patent Act and Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate or dismissal of additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: After the period for making observations, the Commissioner will issue either a certificate of additional term setting out the number of days granted, or a dismissal of the application for additional term if duration is determined to be zero days or less. The Commissioner will provide reasons for the duration or for the dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority references: subsection 46.1(7) and 46.1(5) of the Patent Act; Commissioner must provide reasons (subsection 117.01(8) of the Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional term certificate content
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of additional term must set out the number of days of additional term and include the filing date of the patent application, the title of the invention, and the day on which the certificate is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may correct typographical errors; certificate will be available on the CIPO website (subsection 117.04(1)-(3) of the Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of duration of additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration in the preliminary determination equals the number of days between the Later Date (excluded) and the patent issue date (included), less the number of days to be subtracted under the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: Later Date Jan 20 to Issue Date July 14 = 175 days (Later Date excluded, issue date included) (subsection 46.1(4) Patent Act; section 117.03 Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtracted days general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Days to be subtracted are the total number of days within all applicable periods of time determined under section 117.03 of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtraction reduces the raw interval between Later Date and issue date; see enumerated periods in section 117.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods of time – general counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be multiple applicable periods; a particular period may apply more than once; days may overlap between periods but a calendar day may be subtracted only once. The number of days in any given period includes the first day but does not include the last day. If period ends on or before it begins, its length is zero. If a period does not end before patent is issued, it ends on the date of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: subsections 117.03(2), (5), (6), (10), (11) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of request-for-examination timing on subtraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The period beginning on the applicable day in subsection 46.1(2) and ending on the earlier of a compliant request for examination and the day the application is deemed abandoned will be subtracted; but if the Later Date is determined to be the third anniversary of the request-for-examination date (rather than the fifth anniversary of the applicable day), then subtracted days do not include any period prior to the request-for-examination date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(k) and subsection 117.03(8) of the Patent Rules: special rule to avoid double-counting pre-request intervals when Later Date is tied to the request-for-examination anniversary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods during which application is deemed abandoned are subtracted
rubrics_metrics.description: Any period of time during which an application is deemed abandoned will be subtracted from the duration calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(x) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of granted extensions of time
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension under subsection 3(1) of the Patent Rules is granted, the period begins on the original deadline and ends on the earlier of the day the action is taken and the last day of the extension; that period is subtractable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(j) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods of time – notices general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When a notice is sent to an applicant or other person requiring action, the days in the applicable period beginning on the date of the notice will generally be subtracted; depending on the notice type the period ends on a specified day or the earlier of specified days. The Rules also identify subtraction rules where a notice is withdrawn or where a notice was erroneously not sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 32.04.03 describes how different notices create subtractable periods per paragraph(s) 117.03(1)(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of non-compliance period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of non-compliance is sent under section 65 of the Patent Rules, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earlier of the day on which the applicant replies to the notice in good faith and the day the application is deemed abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(a) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of missing application fee period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requiring payment of the application fee is sent under subsection 27(7) of the Patent Act, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the day of payment of the application fee and late fee, or if paid on different days, the later of those days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(d) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation notice period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requiring translation of the specification is sent under subsection 15(4) of the Patent Rules, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earlier of the day the applicant complies and the day the application is deemed abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(e) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring copy of priority application period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requiring a copy of the priority application is sent under subsection 74(4), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earliest of (1) day a certified copy and certificate of filing date is provided or access provided in DAS, (2) day applicant meets conditions in paragraphs 74(6)(a) and (b), (3) day request for priority is withdrawn, (4) two months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(h) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring translation of priority application period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requiring translation of the priority application is sent under subsection 76(1) or (2), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earliest of (1) day of compliance, (2) day the request for priority is withdrawn, (3) four months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(i) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requisition or final action period
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner’s requisition or final action is sent under subsections 85(1),(2), 86(2),(5), or section 94 of the Patent Rules, the period begins on the date of the requisition and ends on the earlier of the day the applicant replies in good faith and the day the application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 73(1)(a) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(l) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring request for continued examination period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requiring the applicant to request continued examination was sent under subsection 85.1(1), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earlier of a compliant request for continued examination and the day the application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(e) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(m) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allowance period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of allowance is sent under subsection 86(1),(6),(10) or (12), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earliest of day of payment of final fee, day notice is set aside under subsection 85.1(4), day application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(f), and date of withdrawal from allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(q) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional notice of allowance period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a conditional notice of allowance is sent under subsection 86(1.1), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earliest of day of a reply in good faith and payment of the final fee, day notice is set aside under subsection 85.1(4), day application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(g), and date of withdrawal of conditional allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(r) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice indicating submissions or proposed amendments period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice indicating submissions or proposed amendments may be made by a specified day is sent on or after the Commissioner sends a notice that a rejection is not withdrawn, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earliest of day the applicant notifies in writing they will not make a submission, day the submission or proposed amendment is submitted, and the specified day (or later day if extended by the Commissioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(s) of the Patent Rules; applies when sent on/after rejection non-withdrawal notice under paragraph 86(7)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed hearing period (rescheduled)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed hearing date notice is sent on or after the Commissioner’s non-withdrawal-of-rejection notice, and the hearing is rescheduled at the applicant's request, the period begins on the date of the proposed hearing and ends on the earlier of the rescheduled hearing date and the day the applicant notifies the Commissioner in writing they wish to cancel the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(t) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice that amendments must be made period
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after review of a rejected application, a notice under subsection 86(11) informs the applicant that amendments must be made and the applicant makes amendments after that date (other than in response to a final action), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earlier of the day the amendments are received and three months after the date of that notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(u) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring appointment of a patent agent period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice requiring the appointment of a patent agent is sent, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earlier of the day the applicant complies with the notice and the day the application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(y) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of disregarded communication (joint applicant) period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of disregarded communication is sent under subsection 40(1) to a joint applicant who is not the common representative, the period begins on receipt of the written communication and ends on the earliest of (1) first day the joint applicant is appointed as common representative and a request made that Commissioner have regard to the communication, (2) day joint applicant submits written request that Commissioner not have regard, (3) three months after the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of disregarded communication (patent agent) period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of disregarded communication is sent under subsection 41(1) to a patent agent who is not appointed to represent the applicant, the period begins on receipt of the written communication and ends on the earliest of (1) first day the patent agent is appointed and a request made that Commissioner have regard, (2) day applicant submits written request Commissioner not have regard, (3) three months after the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z.01) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of disregarded communication (patent agent not named) period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice is sent under subsection 41.1(2) to the sender of a communication in which a patent agent is not named, the period begins on receipt and ends on earliest of (1) first day the patent agent provides their name and requests Commissioner have regard, (2) day applicant submits written request Commissioner not have regard, (3) three months after the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z.02) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to establish entitlement to PCT national phase application period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice is sent under subsection 154(7) requiring establishment of applicant identity or legal representative, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the day the person complies with the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z.03) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring a translation or complete copy (PCT national phase) period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice is sent under subsection 155.5(6) requiring translation of parts or a complete copy of translated parts of a PCT national phase application, the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earlier of the day the applicant complies and the day the application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z.04) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other notices period (catch-all)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice is sent under any provision of the Patent Act or Rules requiring action within a specified period (other than specified enumerated notices), the period begins on the date of the notice and ends on the earliest of day applicant complies or replies in good faith, the final day of the specified period, and, if applicable, the day the application is deemed abandoned because of failure to act or reply in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z.09) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn notices treated as never sent (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a communication by the Commissioner or Patent Office is withdrawn following an applicant's request in certain circumstances, the communication is considered never to have been sent for purposes of determining periods to subtract, except for purposes of determining specified periods under paragraphs 117.03(1)(z.05)-(z.07).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs 117.03(1)(z.05)-(z.07) and subsection 117.03(9) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices recorded but not sent due to office error
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice appears in the records but was not sent due to a Patent Office error, a period will be subtracted per paragraph 117.03(1)(z.08), unless the applicant notifies the Commissioner in writing that they did not receive the notice and on the same day files a statement notifying without undue delay after becoming aware of the notice and non-receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 117.03(12) of the Patent Rules; cross-ref sections 12.04.03 and 2.02.09 of the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods of time – other events (non-notice events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain application-phase or prosecution events not related to notices will create subtractable periods of time (these are enumerated separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces section 32.04.04 which lists specific non-notice events that give rise to subtractable periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for further drawings period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner requires further drawings under subsection 27(5.2) of the Patent Act, the period begins on the date the request is made and ends on the earlier of the day the applicant responds in good faith and the day the application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(b) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees unpaid period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a maintenance fee was not paid on or before the prescribed date, the period begins on the prescribed day to pay the fee and ends on the earlier of day of payment of the maintenance fee and late fee, and day the application is deemed abandoned under paragraph 73(1)(c) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(f) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of missing parts period
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files an addition and statement under subsection 28.01(1), the period begins on the filing date of the application and ends on the later of the day of receipt of the addition and the statement, and the day the addition is withdrawn, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(g) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for further examination or continued examination period (pre-Oct 3, 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant requested further examination prior to Oct 3, 2022 or requested continued examination, the period begins on the day of the request and ends on the day of payment of the final fee, or if the final fee has been refunded, the day the final fee was paid again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(n) of the Patent Rules (transitional rule for older requests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three examiner notices sent (pre-Oct 3, 2022) period
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on or before Oct 2, 2022, a compliant request for examination was made and a total of three examiner notices were sent under subsection 86(2) or 86(5) before a notice of allowance, the period begins on the date of the third such notice and ends on the day of payment of the final fee (or day final fee paid again if refunded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(o) of the Patent Rules (transitional provision linked to older prosecution practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interviews period
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in an examiner-initiated interview, the applicant agreed to consider making an amendment to correct defects by a specified day, the period begins on the date of the interview and ends on the earliest of day applicant communicates in writing they will not make the amendment, day amendment is received, and the specified day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(p) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction to limit claims period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner directed the applicant to limit the claims to one invention only, the period begins on the date of direction and ends on the earlier of day the applicant replied and the due date of the direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(v) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court proceedings period
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant appeals a refusal under section 41 or applies for judicial review, the period begins on the date of the notice of refusal or issuance of the notice of application for judicial review and ends on the date of the court outcome described in paragraphs 117.03(1)(w),(z.1) (e.g., final judgment, discontinuance). If a court orders a stay of examination/prosecution, the period begins on the day the order is made and ends when the stay is no longer in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs 117.03(1)(w) and (z.11) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated days subtracted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may designate a day during which Patent Office operations are significantly disrupted; all designated days are subtracted in calculating additional term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 117.03(1)(z.12) and subsection 117.03(3) of the Patent Rules; list of designated days published on CIPO website (subsection 117.03(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of additional term — scope and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may reconsider the duration of an additional term; reconsideration can only shorten the duration (cannot lengthen). It may be initiated by the Commissioner or on application by any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 46.3(1),(4) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration initiated by the Commissioner — fee and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner-initiated reconsideration may occur where an error in the duration calculation is suspected; no fee applies for Commissioner-initiated reconsiderations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 32.05.01: procedural note that Commissioner may act sua sponte when suspecting a calculation error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration on application — required contents and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reconsideration (any time on or after grant) must be in writing and contain the patent number, information demonstrating the additional term granted is longer than authorized, and an opinion regarding the duration that should have been made by the Commissioner. The application must be accompanied by the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 117.11(1)-(2) of the Patent Rules and subsection 46.3(2) of the Patent Act. If requirements not met, applicant is informed and may submit missing requirements; Commissioner may stay reconsideration pending court proceedings (subsection 46.3(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of preliminary determination on reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: After a compliant application for reconsideration or Commissioner initiation, the patentee (and the person applying, if applicable) will receive a notice indicating whether the duration is longer than authorized and, if so, the shortened duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 117.11(6) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations period on reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee and the person applying for reconsideration may make observations within two months of the notice of preliminary determination; observations will be considered by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 117.11(7) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome after reconsideration — amended certificate or dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: After the period for observations, the Commissioner will either issue an amended certificate reflecting a shortened duration or dismiss the application for reconsideration if it did not result in shortening. The Commissioner will provide reasons for the amended certificate or dismissal to the patentee and, if applicable, to the applicant for reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 46.3(4) of the Patent Act and subsection 117.11(8) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Court order to shorten additional term
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may bring action in Federal Court against a patentee to shorten the duration of an additional term. If the Court finds the duration is longer than authorized, it will shorten the duration by order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 46.4(1)-(2) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended certificate following a Federal Court order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Court shortens duration, a certified copy of the order will be sent to the Commissioner; the Commissioner will issue an amended certificate of additional term based on the Court’s order and send it to the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 46.4(3) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions — purpose and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional provisions in the amended Patent Act and Patent Rules preserve rights and deadlines from previous regimes; transitional provisions (sections 78.1–78.6 and Rules 165–235) define conditions for filing, prosecution and maintenance after the new regime came into force Oct 30, 2019. The Rules define Category 1 (filing date before Oct 1, 1989) and Category 3 (filing date on/after Oct 1, 1996 and before Oct 30, 2019) applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on determining which provisions apply may be by filing date or by date of the event/action; chapter focuses mainly on Category 3 and patents with filing dates before Oct 30, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating with the Patent Office — dates and electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates accorded to communications are governed by the Patent Rules in effect on that date. As of Oct 30, 2019, section 8.1 of the Patent Act and subsection 10(4) of the Patent Rules allow establishing a date of receipt for communications submitted electronically even on days the Office is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 2 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of documents under former rules (Category 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under former Patent Rules, the Commissioner must have regard to documents in a language other than English or French if submitted or made available with respect to Category 3 applications in specified circumstances (e.g., copy of previously filed application/reference to a digital library; prior art requisition; copy of international application; certified copy of priority document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to former rules: subsection 196(1), subsection 29(1), paragraph 58(1)(a), sections 89 and 180 of the former Patent Rules; see section 215 of the former Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional extension of time for pre-Oct 30 requisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may authorize extensions of time for certain requisitions sent before Oct 30, 2019 where the time to respond in good faith ends after that date (e.g., examiner's requisition with shorter period, requisitions under former sections 23,25,37,94).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be submitted before expiry, pay prescribed fee, provide a simple justification (no affidavit/evidence required). Office will assess and generally grant up to six months per file/action if compliant and reasonable; applicant notified by letter; see CIPO website for service standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time to 'top-up' small entity fees (transitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Category 3 applications, the Commissioner may grant an extension of time to 'top up' specified fees previously paid at the small entity rate under specified Rules. Requirements are in chapter 2.03.03; Commissioner will not grant extension to top-up fees paid at small entity rate prior to June 2, 2007.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: sections 189, 190, subsection 207(2) and section 211 of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date transitional rule (regular Canadian application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed before Oct 30, 2019 that do not receive a filing date before Oct 30, 2019 will be deemed never to have been filed (section 78.21 of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important transitional protection to preserve pre-existing rights where filing date was not conferred before the coming-into-force date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications transitional rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications submitted before Oct 30, 2019 are not subject to the divisional requirements in section 89 of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251). If presentation-date elements were received and at least one after Oct 30, 2019, the presentation date is the date the last requirement was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: sections 188, 202, 231 of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance requirements transitional overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional provisions in the Patent Rules address compliance requirements for applications; specifics summarized in the manual for Category 3 applications and patents filed before Oct 30, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 33.04 and related subsections for particulars (presentation, parts, sequence listings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and parts of an application (transitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 3 applications may comply with former Patent Rules regarding page numbering of the specification (description and claims) rather than section 193 of the new Rules; pages of description may be numbered separately from pages of claims. Category 3 apps with filing date prior to June 2, 2007 may comply with former sequence listing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional allowance to accommodate older-format filings and sequence listings that pre-date harmonization with PCT formatting (amendments on June 2, 2007).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement or declaration of entitlement (transitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before Oct 30, 2019, an applicant may comply with former requirements for inventor and entitlement information instead of section 54 of the new Rules; PCT national phase applicants may file a declaration of entitlement per PCT Rule 4.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants choosing former compliance must consult the relevant point-in-time version of the former Patent Rules (sections 225–227 and  section references  sections 225–227 of the Patent Rules SOR/2019-251).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment after Oct 30 following failure to respond to former requisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after Oct 30, 2019, an applicant fails to respond in good faith to a requisition sent before Oct 30 under former sections 23,25,37 or 94, section 73 of the former Patent Act (as it read before Oct 30, 2019) will apply to the abandonment resulting from the failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 78.52(2) of the Patent Act: transitional rule preserving the former abandonment mechanism for pre-CIF requisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation transitional — common representative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent applications where joint applicants had no patent agent appointed immediately prior to Oct 30, 2019, a common representative will be appointed by default: (a) if no agent appointed at any time prior to Oct 30, 2019, the authorized correspondent under the former Rules is deemed the common representative; (b) if an agent was appointed but revoked prior to Oct 30, 2019, the joint applicant whose name appears first alphabetically is deemed the common representative. Similar default rules apply to patents for patentees. Joint applicants/patentees may appoint a common representative by submitting a signed notice. Until appointment of a common representative, signatures of all applicants/patentees are required to appoint or revoke an agent (unless agent signs revocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 218 and section 219 of the Patent Rules; section 33.05.01 gives practical instructions on who is deemed common representative in various scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointed patent agents and associate patent agents remain effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appointment of a patent agent or associate patent agent made prior to Oct 30, 2019 in accordance with the former Patent Rules remains in effect after Oct 30, 2019 and is considered to have been made under the new Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 216 and 217 of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251); see Chapter 5 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures related to patents — representation rules not retroactive
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions in the new Patent Rules regarding representation for procedures relating to a granted patent (section 37) will not apply to any procedure that started prior to Oct 30, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 33.05.03 clarifies non-retroactivity for representation provisions that would otherwise affect ongoing procedures started under the former Rules.
